A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TerminalTraj and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering, including the unchanged case studies in v1 Appendix N and v3 Appendix P.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and TerminalBench results, repository and instance-quality analyses, domain ablations, and trajectory-verification experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds size-matched ablations, extended data-scaling results, and teacher–student consistency analyses.

M1.justification: The pipeline, ScoreModel architecture, and training objective are retained. However, v1 Appendix E names Qwen3-Coder-32B as the teacher; v3 Appendix G.2 names Qwen2.5-Coder-32B while its supervision paragraph still names Qwen3-Coder-32B. The PDFs do not resolve whether the teacher changed or the new description is erroneous.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same eight programming languages, eight specialized domains, 50,733 trajectories, and TerminalBench 1.0/2.0 coverage. The added experiments examine existing data and tasks; the new filtering disclosures do not establish a change in corpus coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix G.3 adds direct teacher-model scoring as a comparator for the lightweight ScoreModel, including repository-selection and downstream instance-quality comparisons. The teacher previously appeared as a supervision source. The main model baselines and Nex-N1, SETA, and trajectory-verification comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 9K full-domain control matched to the domain-removed training sets and extends the data-size study beyond 8K to 32K and the full dataset. Teacher–student evaluation introduces 1,000 paired file scores, 40 repositories per score interval per model, and top-50 selection comparisons within 500 repositories. These substantially expand the evaluation design while retaining the main TerminalBench setup.

E4.justification: New Appendices B, C, and G.3 test the training-size confound in domain ablations, possible saturation beyond 8K trajectories, and ScoreModel fidelity through ranking, instance-quality, and selection-overlap analyses. v1 lacked these controls and diagnostic checks. Existing ablations and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four independent benchmark runs and task-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals; v1 Table 7 is retained as v3 Table 10. The added analyses provide point estimates and descriptive agreement metrics, without new uncertainty procedures, significance tests, or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: The main benchmark results remain unchanged, but v3 adds the 9K full-domain score of 29, the 32K-data score of 32, teacher–student quality scores, Spearman correlation of 0.81, and reported top-50 overlap of 85%. It also adds filtering and license statistics. Some new entries are unreconciled with retained plots: Table 3 reports 13 for removing Web Service data, versus approximately 22 in Figure 4.

T1.justification: The repository-score definition in Equation 1, sigmoid regression model, MSE objective, and meaning of pass@k remain unchanged. The revision adds empirical analyses and explanations, without new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: scalable executable trajectory generation, approximately 32K Docker environments, 50,733 trajectories, strong smaller-model performance, and improved test-time sampling. The headline TerminalTraj-32B scores remain 35.30% and 22.00%.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly attributes domain-ablation losses to composition rather than sample count and argues that verified-data benefits continue beyond 8K. It adds the rationale that ScoreModel should preserve useful rankings at lower cost rather than reproduce exact teacher scores. The Ethics Statement adds licensing boundaries and acknowledges imperfect privacy-filter recall.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands documentation with the ScoreModel pseudo-labeling rubric, license-screening criteria, N-gram filtering of copied code, and regex-based privacy filtering. It also changes the stated code/data repository destination. Existing training hyperparameters and generation prompts are retained; the new disclosures do not establish that those procedures were newly implemented, and teacher identity remains inconsistent.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning remain the same. Several references receive publication and bibliographic updates. SETA moves from an author–year reference to a blog footnote, but the same work and comparison remain present.

P1.justification: Section 5.2 is renamed Best-of-K Trajectory Sampling and its introductory explanation is revised. v3 adds Ethics and Conflict of Interest statements, inserts appendix sections, and expands the reward-model appendix into subsections. Author affiliations and publication information change, while most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds three appendix tables for the new analyses and a boxed ScoreModel scoring prompt. Existing tables are relocated and renumbered, with corresponding page reflow. The seven figures retain their visual content, and Table 2 receives a small caption correction.

improvement.justification: The size-matched control, extended scaling study, ScoreModel checks, and filtering disclosures address real gaps in v1. However, new Table 3 conflicts with retained Figure 4, and Table 4 reports 28 at 8K trajectories while Figure 5 shows approximately 30, without explaining different settings. The contradictory teacher-model names further impair reproducibility. These problems affect the new supporting evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
